summary: A 1936 Forest Service steel Aermotor fire lookout on the Kaibab near the South Rim, listed on the NRHP in 1988 and the NHLR in 2001, shown as standing; current access unconfirmed.

facts.design: Aermotor steel tower with a 7 by 7 foot metal cab; historic lookout residence on the site

visit.trail_note: The Arizona Trail passes the tower

events.note: Site was one of the original tower sites selected when the early Grand Canyon National Monument was planned
Forest Service built the 81-foot Aermotor tower with a 7 by 7 foot metal cab, after an earlier platform tower stood on the site
Placed on the National Register of Historic Places January 28, 1988
Registered with the National Historic Lookout Register May 1, 2001; nominated by Dave Lorenz, director of the AZ/NM FFLA

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives the tower as 81 feet (about 24.7 m) and Wikipedia gives 80 feet (24 m). The NHLR registry figure is used for height_m; the story gives both.

notes_for_editor: The core history (1936 build, Forest Service ownership, NRHP 1988, NHLR 2001, standing) is consistent across sources. Staffing history, notable fires and current access or rental status are NOT established: the only pages I could read do not cover them, and the NRHP nomination PDF (NARA) and Living New Deal page returned HTTP 403. Search snippets mention summer staffing and a historical-marker text that gives 1906 for the tower, which conflicts with 1936; neither was verified on a fetched page, so neither is used. Do not confuse with the separate 'Grandview' tree lookout (abandoned) listed on firelookout.org at 35.93278, -111.97889. Suggest checking the Tusayan Ranger District for staffing and access before publishing a 'today' section.
